newsitem.title: LATVIA: ALDARIS HITS ALL-TIME SALES HIGH IN 1996.
newsitem.headline: ALDARIS HITS ALL-TIME SALES HIGH IN 1996.

text.p: Aldaris, largest Latvia's brewery, said it registered 2.381 million lats of net profit in 1996 versus 2.170 million lats in 1995 and reached an all-time high in sales of 39.4 million litres of beer.
Aldaris, like Saku in Estonia and Kalnapilis in Lithuania, is owned by Baltic Beverages, itself owned by Hartwall and Nordic brewer Pripps.
"For 1997, the shareholders' meeting approved figures not lower than those of last year," Vitalii Gavrilov, the brewery's president, told a news conference late on Friday.
"Profits perhaps will be higher than last year's," he added.
Aldaris' market share increased by four percent to 57 percent in Latvia during 1996, including imported produce, while per capita beer consumption slipped to 27 litres from 31 litres.
Aldaris last year re-entered the non-alcocholic drinks market by launching mineral water Vichy in April and sees profits in the growing mineral water market in 1997.
It plans more investment in this area by June.
"There is a definite need for quality mineral water. We have already sold 1.5 times more than budgeted in 1997. We hope to earn on our mineral water," Gavrilov said.
Gavrilov confirmed Aldaris' intentions to become a public company but said it was a matter of time.
He said that Aldaris' operations still had too much of a seasonal character, which might hit the share price.
Aldaris will pay a 10 lat dividend for 1996 versus 5.70 lats in 1995.
Aldaris said it was the second largest brewer in the Baltics after Lithiania'sUtenos, which registered 39.45 million litres of sales.
